statement: Fix the constants D0 and Ctpl in Definition 9.3, and a lower scale threshold n∗ ≥ 1. There is a constant C with the following property. Let Λ be a finite induced subgraph of the square lattice, let A ⊆ Λ, and suppose that b = |∂ΛA| > 0. Let Z be the set of endpoints of those cut edges. There are a set D ⊆ A, a finite ordered collection of disjoint nonempty sets Xi ⊆ A, labels fi ∈ {0, 1}, ambient templates Ti ⊂ Z2, and integers ni ≥ n∗ such that: 1. A = D ˙ ∪ ⋃︁ i Xi and |D| ≤ Cb. 2. Xi ⊆ A ∩ Ti. Each Ti is a template of Definition 9.3: it is a union of Ni lattice samples of closed convex rectangles or triangles with side slopes 0, ∞, 1, −1, each of sup-norm diameter at most si, where diam∞ Ti ≤ ni, ni ≥ CtplNi(si + 1), dist∞(Ti, Z) > 4D0si. Moreover Li = ⌊n1−ℓ i ⌋ ≤ si. 3. The templates satisfy dist∞(Ti, Z) > 2nβ i , (11.3) dist∞ ⎛ ⎜ ⎜ ⎜ ⎝ Ti, ⋃︂ j<i fj=fi Xj ⎞ ⎟ ⎟ ⎟ ⎠ > 2nβ i . (11.4) As usual, the distance to the empty set is infinite. 79 4. The scale losses are summable: ∑︂ i n−100 i ≤ Cb. The constant C may depend on the fixed template constants and on n∗, but not on the domain or cut.
